In systems modeling, particularly when using the concept of stocks and flows, we can represent complex systems in a way that highlights their dynamics, feedback loops, and the accumulation or depletion of resources over time. Let's apply this framework to our discussion on value creation within communities and individual wellbeing, using the stocks and flows concept to reframe our mathematical logic.

\#\#\# Understanding Stocks and Flows

\- \*\*Stocks\*\* represent accumulations of resources or quantities that change over time. In our context, stocks could be individual wellbeing, community value, or contributions to DAOs.  
\- \*\*Flows\*\* are the rates at which these stocks change, either inputs that increase the stock or outputs that decrease it. For example, time spent on personal or community activities can be seen as flows that affect the stocks of wellbeing and community value.

\#\#\# Applying Stocks and Flows to Our Model

1\. \*\*Stocks in the Model:\*\*  
   \- \*\*Wellbeing Stock (\\(W\\))\*\*: This is the accumulation of all factors contributing to an individual's quality of life, such as health, happiness, and personal growth.  
   \- \*\*Community Value Stock (\\(V\_{DAO}\\))\*\*: Represents the accumulated value within each DAO, including knowledge, social capital, and economic assets created through collective efforts.

2\. \*\*Flows Affecting the Stocks:\*\*  
   \- \*\*Time Allocation Flows (\\(T\_{personal}\\), \\(T\_{community}\\))\*\*: The time individuals dedicate to personal wellbeing activities and community contributions acts as flows into the wellbeing and community value stocks, respectively.  
   \- \*\*Contribution Flows (\\(D\_i\\))\*\*: The efforts and activities contributed to each DAO represent flows into the community value stock.

\#\#\# Building the Model with Stocks and Flows

To construct a systems model reflecting our discussions, we consider how flows (time and contributions) impact the stocks (wellbeing and community value) and how these stocks interact within the system.

\- \*\*Modeling Wellbeing as a Stock:\*\*  
  Wellbeing increases with personal time investment (\\(T\_{personal}\\)) but may also be influenced by contributions to community activities (\\(T\_{community}\\)) that provide personal fulfillment or stress. An exponential function might model the non-linear impact of these time allocations on wellbeing.

\- \*\*Modeling Community Value as a Stock:\*\*  
  Community value grows with contributions (\\(D\_i\\)) from individuals. The relationship can be non-linear, where initial contributions significantly impact but may exhibit diminishing returns as the community matures.

\- \*\*Feedback Loops:\*\*  
  Feedback loops are crucial in stock and flow systems. For instance, an increase in community value (stock) could lead to increased individual wellbeing (stock) due to a sense of accomplishment and belonging, creating a positive feedback loop.

\- \*\*Visual Representation:\*\*  
  In a diagram, stocks could be represented as rectangles, flows as arrows feeding into or out of these stocks, and feedback loops as circular paths that connect stocks through flows.

\#\#\# Final Systems Model

In our final model, we would have:

\- Two main stocks: Wellbeing (\\(W\\)) and Community Value (\\(V\_{DAO}\\)).  
\- Flows into these stocks: Time allocations (\\(T\_{personal}\\) and \\(T\_{community}\\)) and contributions (\\(D\_i\\)).  
\- Feedback loops illustrating how increased community value enhances individual wellbeing, which in turn motivates further contributions to the community.

This stock and flow model provides a dynamic view of the interactions between individual actions and community outcomes. It highlights the importance of balancing contributions and personal time to sustain wellbeing and grow community value, acknowledging the complex feedback mechanisms that regulate these systems.

Translating the stocks and flows concept into mathematical terms for our discussion involves defining equations that represent how the stocks (wellbeing and community value) change over time based on the flows (time allocations and contributions). We'll integrate feedback loops explicitly into these equations to capture the dynamic interplay between individual wellbeing and community value.

\#\#\# Defining the Stocks and Flows Mathematically

1\. \*\*Stocks:\*\*  
   \- \*\*Wellbeing (\\(W\\))\*\*: The cumulative measure of an individual's quality of life.  
   \- \*\*Community Value (\\(V\_{DAO}\\))\*\*: The total accumulated value created within a DAO.

2\. \*\*Flows:\*\*  
   \- \*\*Time Allocation to Personal Wellbeing (\\(T\_{personal}\\))\*\*: Time spent on activities that directly contribute to \\(W\\).  
   \- \*\*Time Allocation to Community Contributions (\\(T\_{community}\\))\*\*: Time dedicated to DAO activities, affecting \\(V\_{DAO}\\).  
   \- \*\*Contributions (\\(C\\))\*\*: Efforts and activities contributing to \\(V\_{DAO}\\), which can be influenced by \\(W\\) (reflecting the motivation or capacity to contribute).

\#\#\# Mathematical Representation

\- \*\*Change in Wellbeing Stock (\\(\\Delta W\\))\*\* over time is a function of personal time investment minus the potential drain from excessive community contributions:  
    
  \\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- g(T\_{community}) \+ h(V\_{DAO}) \\\]  
    
  Here, \\(f(T\_{personal})\\) represents the growth in wellbeing from personal activities, \\(g(T\_{community})\\) captures any negative impact from overcommitment to community efforts, and \\(h(V\_{DAO})\\) indicates the positive feedback from community value on individual wellbeing.

\- \*\*Change in Community Value Stock (\\(\\Delta V\_{DAO}\\))\*\* is a function of the contributions made, influenced by the current state of wellbeing:  
    
  \\\[ \\frac{dV\_{DAO}}{dt} \= k(C(W)) \\\]  
    
  \\(k(C(W))\\) reflects the contributions to the community value, which are dependent on the wellbeing (\\(W\\)) of the contributors, signifying that happier, more fulfilled individuals are likely to contribute more effectively.

![][image29]

\#\#\# Incorporating Feedback Loops

The term \\(h(V\_{DAO})\\) in the wellbeing equation introduces a feedback loop, illustrating how an increase in community value enhances individual wellbeing. This is crucial for capturing the dynamic interactions and mutual influence between individual and community growth.

\#\#\# Simplifying Assumptions

To model this system more concretely, one might make specific assumptions or choose functional forms for \\(f\\), \\(g\\), \\(h\\), and \\(k\\). For instance:

\- \*\*Linear Relationships\*\*: Initially assuming linear relationships for simplicity, where each hour of personal time or community contribution directly adds to or subtracts from the stocks.  
\- \*\*Exponential or Logarithmic Functions\*\*: For a more nuanced model that captures diminishing returns or accelerated growth, exponential or logarithmic functions could replace linear functions.

\#\#\# Conclusion

This mathematical framework for stocks and flows in the context of wellbeing and community value offers a structured way to analyze and understand the complex dynamics at play. It highlights the importance of balance and feedback in sustaining both individual fulfillment and communal prosperity. Adjusting the specific functions and parameters based on empirical data or simulations can refine the model, tailoring it to specific communities or DAOs.

\#\#\# Step 1: Defining the Basic Components

\*\*Stocks:\*\*   
\- \*\*Wellbeing (\\(W\\))\*\*: The accumulated state of individual health, happiness, and satisfaction.  
\- \*\*Community Value (\\(V\_{DAO}\\))\*\*: The total accumulated contributions and value within the DAO.

\*\*Flows:\*\*   
\- \*\*Personal Time Investment (\\(T\_{personal}\\))\*\*: Time spent on activities that directly increase \\(W\\).  
\- \*\*Community Contribution Time (\\(T\_{community}\\))\*\*: Time dedicated to DAO activities, influencing \\(V\_{DAO}\\).

\#\#\# Explanation:  
Think of \\(W\\) and \\(V\_{DAO}\\) as two tanks of water. \\(T\_{personal}\\) is like pouring water into your personal tank (\\(W\\)), increasing your wellbeing. \\(T\_{community}\\) is like pouring water into a communal tank (\\(V\_{DAO}\\)), enhancing community value.

\#\#\# Step 2: Incorporating Change Over Time

We model how \\(W\\) and \\(V\_{DAO}\\) change over time due to the flows of time investment and contributions:

\\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- g(T\_{community}) \\\]  
\\\[ \\frac{dV\_{DAO}}{dt} \= h(T\_{community}) \\\]

\#\#\# Explanation:  
The rate at which the water level in your personal tank (\\(W\\)) changes depends on how much water you add (\\(f(T\_{personal})\\)) and how much you divert to the communal tank (\\(g(T\_{community})\\)). For the communal tank (\\(V\_{DAO}\\)), the rate of change depends on the collective effort poured into it (\\(h(T\_{community})\\)).  
![][image30]  
\#\#\# Step 3: Modeling Feedback Loops

We introduce feedback loops to reflect how the state of one stock influences the other:

\- \*\*Positive Feedback on Wellbeing from Community Value\*\*: The more value the community generates (\\(V\_{DAO}\\)), the greater the individual's sense of fulfillment and wellbeing (\\(W\\)).

\\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- g(T\_{community}) \+ \\alpha \\cdot V\_{DAO} \\\]

\#\#\# Explanation:  
As the communal tank fills (increasing \\(V\_{DAO}\\)), it starts to overflow back into your personal tank (\\(W\\)), symbolizing increased wellbeing from your contributions to the community.

![][image31]

\#\#\# Step 4: Addressing Non-linearity and Saturation

Recognizing that relationships are not always linear, especially at extreme values, we adjust our model to include non-linear dynamics, such as saturation effects:

\\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- g(T\_{community}) \+ \\alpha \\cdot \\ln(1 \+ V\_{DAO}) \\\]  
\\\[ \\frac{dV\_{DAO}}{dt} \= \\beta \\cdot \\tanh(h(T\_{community})) \\\]

\#\#\# Explanation:  
The logarithmic term for wellbeing feedback (\\(\\ln(1 \+ V\_{DAO})\\)) suggests that the initial contributions significantly boost wellbeing, but the effect tapers off. The hyperbolic tangent (\\(\\tanh\\)) for community contributions indicates that there's an optimal level of contribution that maximizes community value without leading to burnout.  
![][image32]  
\#\#\# Step 5: Integrating Multiple DAOs and Contributions

For individuals engaged with multiple DAOs, we extend the model to account for diverse contributions and their cumulative impact on wellbeing and each DAO's value:

\\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- \\sum\_{i=1}^{N} g(T\_{community\_i}) \+ \\sum\_{i=1}^{N} \\alpha\_i \\cdot \\ln(1 \+ V\_{DAO\_i}) \\\]  
\\\[ \\frac{dV\_{DAO\_i}}{dt} \= \\beta\_i \\cdot \\tanh(h(T\_{community\_i})) \\\]  
![][image33]  
\#\#\# Explanation:  
Imagine having several communal tanks, each representing a different DAO. You decide how much water to contribute to each based on your capacity and the unique benefits you derive from them. The overall level in your personal wellbeing tank reflects not just one but the combined overflow from all communal tanks you contribute to.

\#\#\# Conclusion:

This step-by-step buildup introduces the stocks and flows model as a powerful tool for understanding and optimizing the dynamics of individual wellbeing and community value creation. By incorporating feedback loops, non-linear dynamics, and the complexity of engaging with multiple DAOs, we achieve a comprehensive system model that captures the essence of participatory communities in the Internet of Value.

\#\#\# Intellectual Debate on the Proposed Model

\#\#\#\# Critique: Complexity vs. Real-World Application

\*\*Critique\*\*: While the model intricately captures the dynamics between individual wellbeing and community value, its complexity could deter real-world application. The inclusion of non-linear dynamics, multiple DAOs, and feedback loops, although academically rigorous, might pose challenges for practical implementation. How do we ensure that this model doesn’t remain theoretical but can be applied and tested in real communities?

\*\*Defense\*\*: The complexity of the model mirrors the complexity of human behavior and community interactions. By breaking down the model into component parts (stocks, flows, feedback loops), we provide a framework that can be adapted and scaled according to the specific needs and capacities of different DAOs. Moreover, the model's complexity is a strength, allowing for the simulation of various scenarios and interventions, leading to insights that simpler models could overlook. Practical application is feasible through stepwise implementation and leveraging technology for data collection and analysis.

\#\#\#\# Critique: Quantification of Wellbeing

\*\*Critique\*\*: The model’s approach to quantifying wellbeing and community contributions might oversimplify these inherently qualitative experiences. Can numerical values truly capture the nuanced impact of community engagement on individual wellbeing?

\*\*Defense\*\*: Quantification serves as a tool for visibility and measurement, not as a replacement for qualitative experiences. By assigning values to wellbeing and contributions, we aim to highlight patterns, identify disparities, and measure progress over time. It encourages a data-informed approach to enhancing community structures and personal wellbeing strategies. Furthermore, the model is designed to be supplemented with qualitative feedback mechanisms, ensuring a holistic understanding of community and individual health.

\#\#\#\# Critique: Ethical Considerations

\*\*Critique\*\*: The mathematical model, with its focus on optimizing individual wellbeing and community value, might inadvertently prioritize efficiency or productivity over genuine human experiences. How does the model account for ethical considerations, ensuring it promotes a balanced and humane approach to community engagement?

\*\*Defense\*\*: Ethical considerations are central to the model's design and implementation. The inclusion of feedback loops and non-linear dynamics specifically addresses concerns about burnout and the law of diminishing returns. The model advocates for a balanced approach to personal and community activities, emphasizing sustainability and long-term wellbeing. Ethical guidelines and governance structures within DAOs can further ensure the model is applied in a way that respects individual limits and promotes collective welfare.

\#\#\#\# Critique: Adaptability to Different Community Structures

\*\*Critique\*\*: Communities and DAOs are diverse in their goals, values, and structures. Can a single model, even one as comprehensive as this, adequately reflect the vast diversity of community ecosystems?

\*\*Defense\*\*: The model’s foundational principles are designed to be universally applicable, yet flexible enough to be tailored to specific community contexts. The variables and functions within the model (e.g., \\(f(T\_{personal})\\), \\(g(T\_{community})\\), \\(\\alpha\_i\\)) can be customized to reflect the unique dynamics and priorities of different DAOs. This adaptability is a strength, allowing the model to serve as a conceptual framework that guides tailored strategies for community engagement and wellbeing enhancement.

\#\#\# Conclusion

The debate highlights the balance between theoretical complexity and practical application, the challenge of quantifying qualitative experiences, the imperative of ethical considerations, and the model’s adaptability to diverse community ecosystems. The model is proposed as a starting point, a framework for understanding and enhancing the interplay between individual wellbeing and community value creation in a way that is informed, balanced, and ethically sound. Its ultimate test lies in iterative applications, refinements, and the integration of both quantitative and qualitative insights.

# Better Math: {#better-math:}

Certainly\! Let's compile and structure the mathematical model we've developed to articulate the concept of Value Created (VC) within the framework of The Internet of Value, including the dynamics of individual wellbeing and community value across multiple DAOs.

\#\#\# 1\. Overall Value Created (VC)

The overarching measure, Value Created (\\(VC(t)\\)), encapsulates the combined effect of individual wellbeing and the collective value generated within communities or DAOs over time:

\\\[ VC(t) \= \\lambda \\left( \\frac{dW}{dt} \\right) \+ \\sum\_{i=1}^{N} \\mu\_i \\left( \\frac{dV\_{DAO\_i}}{dt} \\right) \\\]

\#\#\# 2\. Rate of Change in Individual Wellbeing (\\(dW/dt\\))

The rate of change in individual wellbeing (\\(dW/dt\\)) is influenced by personal time investment, community contribution time, and the feedback from community value:

\\\[ \\frac{dW}{dt} \= f(T\_{personal}) \- \\sum\_{i=1}^{N} g\_i(T\_{community\_i}) \+ \\sum\_{i=1}^{N} \\alpha\_i \\cdot \\ln(1 \+ V\_{DAO\_i}) \\\]

\- \*\*\\(f(T\_{personal})\\)\*\*: Represents the positive impact of personal activities on wellbeing.  
\- \*\*\\(g\_i(T\_{community\_i})\\)\*\*: Captures the potential negative impact of overcommitting time to community contributions on individual wellbeing.  
\- \*\*\\(\\alpha\_i \\cdot \\ln(1 \+ V\_{DAO\_i})\\)\*\*: Reflects the positive feedback from contributing to and participating in community value.

\#\#\# 3\. Rate of Change in Community Value (\\(dV\_{DAO\_i}/dt\\))

The rate of change in community value for each DAO (\\(i\\)) over time is determined by the contributions made by individuals:

\\\[ \\frac{dV\_{DAO\_i}}{dt} \= \\beta\_i \\cdot \\tanh(h\_i(T\_{community\_i})) \\\]

\- \*\*\\(\\beta\_i \\cdot \\tanh(h\_i(T\_{community\_i}))\\)\*\*: Models the efficiency and impact of contributions to the DAO, incorporating non-linear dynamics to capture diminishing returns or accelerated growth.

\#\#\# Coefficients and Functions

\- \*\*\\(\\lambda\\), \\(\\mu\_i\\)\*\*: Weighting coefficients that balance the contributions to wellbeing and community value in the VC metric.  
\- \*\*\\(N\\)\*\*: Represents the number of DAOs an individual contributes to.  
\- \*\*\\(f\\), \\(g\_i\\), \\(h\_i\\)\*\*: Are functions describing the relationships between time investments, contributions, and their impacts on wellbeing and community value.

This concise mathematical framework provides a structured approach to understanding the complex dynamics of value creation within skill-based economic institutions and communities. It highlights the importance of individual contributions to personal wellbeing and community value, advocating for a balanced and equitable distribution of the value created. By capturing these dynamics quantitatively, the model offers insights into optimizing engagement and contributions for sustainable and inclusive growth.

3\. \*\*Adjusting for Activity Type\*\*:  
   \- \*\*Earning\*\*: Valued at 100% of the hourly rate or more.  
   \- \*\*Learning and Community Building\*\*: Initially proposed at 100% of a "floor" hourly rate, with the understanding that all activities contribute towards the DAO's value.

4\. \*\*Revised Valuation Based on Discussion\*\*:  
   \- \*\*Earning Activities\*\*: Maintain at 100% or potentially higher.  
   \- \*\*Learning and Community Building\*\*: These activities are also valued at 100% of the hourly rate, reflecting their intrinsic value to personal development and the DAO's social fabric.

\#\#\# Non-Performance-Related Activities

5\. \*\*Wellbeing Improvement Matrix\*\*:  
   Creating a matrix to quantify improvements in wellbeing across different nodes (Physiology, Emotions, Feelings, Thoughts, Habits), excluding Performance.

6\. \*\*Matrix Structure\*\*:  
   Rows represent BWS ranges (100-1000), and columns represent the five wellbeing nodes. Values in the matrix suggest maximum improvement percentages, which are higher for lower BWS ranges and decrease as BWS increases, reflecting the challenge of making significant improvements at higher wellbeing levels.

| BWS Range | Physiology | Emotions | Feelings | Thoughts | Habits |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 100-200 | \+5% | \+5% | \+5% | \+5% | \+5% |
| 201-300 | \+4% | \+4% | \+4% | \+4% | \+4% |
| 301-400 | \+3% | \+3% | \+3% | \+3% | \+3% |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
| 901-1000 | \+1% | \+1% | \+1% | \+1% | \+1% |

7\. \*\*Calculating VC for Non-Performance Activities\*\*:  
   [![][image43]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C%5B%20VC_%7BNon-Performance%7D%20%3D%20BWS%20%2B%20%5Csum%20\(%5Ctext%7BImprovement%20values%20from%20each%20Wellbeing%20Node%7D\)%20%5C%5D#0)  
   This formula considers daily improvements or declines across wellbeing nodes, using the BWS as a base and adjusting for improvements measured through the wellbeing matrix.

\#\#\# Incorporating Daily Improvement and Normalization

8\. \*\*Daily Improvement Percentage (DIP)\*\* for non-performance activities, and normalization of [![][image44]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C\(V_%7BDAO%7D%5C\)#0) for performance activities, allowing for a dynamic assessment of value creation based on daily activities.

\#\#\# Final Model Synthesis

9\. \*\*Comprehensive VC Calculation\*\* combines the performance and non-performance aspects, recognizing the interdependent and dynamic nature of value creation within communities or DAOs.

This model provides a holistic approach to understanding and quantifying the contributions of individuals to their personal wellbeing and community engagement. It recognizes the complex interplay between various activities and their impact on an individual's capacity to generate value, offering a nuanced perspective that goes beyond traditional economic or productivity metrics.

## 1\. \*\*Overall Value Created (VC):\*\* {#1.-**overall-value-created-(vc):**}

  [![][image45]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20VC%20%3D%20W%20%5Ctimes%20V_%7Bcom%7D%20#0)  
   \- \*\*Variables:\*\*  
     \- [![][image46]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20W%20%5C\)%20#0): Wellbeing Score \[Inherent Value of the Individual\]  
     \-  [![][image47]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C\(%20V_%7Bcom%7D%20%5C\)%20#0): Value for Community (value created within and derived from the community)

 \*\*Explanation:\*\*  
   \- The overall value capture is a function of the individual's wellbeing score and the value they contribute to their community.  
   \- This formula represents a holistic measurement of value created (VC).

## 2\.  Baseline Wellbeing Score Calculation: {#2.-baseline-wellbeing-score-calculation:}

The Baseline Wellbeing Score is a function of Physiology, Emotions, Feelings , Thoughts, Habits and Performance

\*\*Wellbeing Improvement Matrix (WIM):\*\*  
Each dimension is measured through specific metrics:  
\- \*\*Physiology:\*\* Movement, Sleep, Diet, Breathwork  
\- \*\*Emotions:\*\* Meditation, Mood Meter Usage, Gratitude List  
\- \*\*Feelings:\*\* Meditation, Gratitude List, Awareness  
\- \*\*Thoughts:\*\* Journaling, Dream Log, Biases Awareness  
\- \*\*Habits:\*\* Positive/Negative Valence, Habit Formation  
\- \*\*\* Performance: \*\* \- Financial Data (Salary, etc \- Credit Score)

## 3\. \*\*Time-Based Value Capture (VC) (Integral Form):\*\* {#3.-**time-based-value-capture-(vc)-(integral-form):**}

   [![][image48]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C%5B%20VC\(t_%7Bstart%7D%2C%20t_%7Bend%7D\)%20%3D%20%5Cint_%7Bt_%7Bstart%7D%7D%5E%7Bt_%7Bend%7D%7D%20W\(t\)%20%5Ctimes%20V_%7Bcom%7D\(t\)%20%5C%2C%20dt%20%5C%5D%20#0)  
   \- \*\*Variables:\*\*  
     \- [![][image49]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20t_%7Bstart%7D%20%5C\)%20#0): Start of the time period  
     \- [![][image50]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20t_%7Bend%7D%20%5C\)%20#0): End of the time period  
     \-  [![][image51]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C\(%20W\(t\)%20%5C\)%20#0): Wellbeing Score as a function of time  
     \-  [![][image52]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C\(%20V_%7Bcom%7D\(t\)%20%5C\)%20#0): Community Value as a function of time

\*\*Explanation:\*\*  
   \- This formula captures value created over a specific time period by integrating wellbeing and community value over time.

## 4\. \*\*Performance vs. Non-Performance Value Capture:\*\* {#4.-**performance-vs.-non-performance-value-capture:**}

 [![][image53]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%20%5C%5B%20VC%20%3D%20VC_%7Bperformance%7D%20%2B%20VC_%7Bnon-performance%7D%20%5C%5D%20#0)  
   \- \*\*Variables:\*\*  
     \-[![][image54]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20VC_%7Bperformance%7D%20%5C\)%20#0): Value created from performance activities  
     \-[![][image55]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20VC_%7Bnon-performance%7D%20%5C\)#0): Value created from non-performance activities

   \*\*Explanation:\*\*  
   \- Total value capture is the sum of value derived from performance activities (any time logged within a community i.e. tagged as performance within the wellbeing protocol stack ) and non-performance activities (personal wellbeing related activities such as Physiology, Emotions, Feelings, Thoughts, Habits).

## 5\. \*\*Performance Value Capture (VCp):\*\* {#5.-**performance-value-capture-(vcp):**}

[![][image56]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%20%20%5C%5B%20VC_%7Bperformance%7D%20%3D%20W_%7Bnormalized%7D%20%5Ctimes%20\(%5Ctext%7BPer%20Hour%20Rate%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Ctext%7BTime%20Spent%7D\)%20%5C%5D#0)  
   \- \*\*Variables:\*\*  
     \- [![][image57]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%5C\(%20W_%7Bnormalized%7D%20%5C\)#0): Normalized Wellbeing Score  
     \- \*\*Per Hour Rate:\*\* Compensation rate based on skills and reputation  
     \- \*\*Time Spent:\*\* Amount of time dedicated to performance activities  
  \*\*Assumptions:\*\*  
   \- The Per Hour Rate is predefined by the community based on the individual's skill level  
   \- Time Spent is measured in hours.

\*\*Explanation:\*\*  
   \- This formula calculates the value captured from performance activities by normalizing the wellbeing score and multiplying it by the per-hour compensation rate and the time spent.

## 6\. \*\*Non-Performance Value Capture (VCnp):\*\* {#6.-**non-performance-value-capture-(vcnp):**}

  [![][image58]](http://www.sciweavers.org/tex2img.php?bc=Transparent&fc=Black&im=jpg&fs=100&ff=modern&edit=0&eq=%20%5C%5B%20VC_%7Bnon-performance%7D%20%3D%20W%20%5C%5D#0)  
   \- \*\*Variables:\*\*  
     \-[![][image59]](http://www.sciweavers.org/tex2img.php?bc=Transparent&fc=Black&im=jpg&fs=100&ff=modern&edit=0&eq=%20%20%20-%24%24#0) [![][image60]](https://www.codecogs.com/eqnedit.php?latex=%20%5C\(%20W%20%5C\)%20#0): Wellbeing Score

Non-performance value capture is directly proportional to the individual's wellbeing score, representing the intrinsic value of their involvement in non-performance activities.

# VHTTP vs HTTP: The Human-Centric Protocol for Value Capture and Exchange

In the evolution from traditional data-centric protocols like HTTP to a human-centric framework, VHTTP (Valuable Human Time Transfer Protocol) redefines how value is exchanged within decentralized communities. 

Unlike HTTP, which enables the transfer of information across the web, VHTTP focuses on the **transfer of human value**—specifically time, skills, and wellbeing. This protocol captures, validates, and rewards individual contributions based on **time slots**, **community participation**, and **wellbeing scores**, making it an essential component in the Internet of Value ecosystem. 

Through VHTTP, contributors are empowered to engage in **earning**, **learning**, and **community-building**, where **value capture** is linked directly to their activities and their **impact on the community**.

| Aspect | HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) | VHTTP (Valuable Human Time Transfer Protocol) |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Core Purpose | Transfers and retrieves data over the internet | Facilitates human time, skill, and wellbeing exchanges within decentralized communities |
| Key Activity | Request-Response cycle (GET, POST, etc.) | Submit Time Slot (start time, end time, activity, proof of activity) |
| Value Transferred | Data (web pages, media, files) | Human value: time spent, wellbeing, skills, community contribution |
| Participants | Client (browser) and Server (web hosting) | Individual contributors, community validators, and platforms |
| Authentication | Typically session-based (cookies, tokens) | Human verification via skill-based community validation (earning, learning, or community-building) |
| Proof of Work | None | Proof of Activity (POA): tangible evidence (file links, deliverables, etc.) |
| Verification Layer | Server responses with status codes (200 OK, 404 Not Found, etc.) | Community-based validation of time slots and activities through SAOcommons |
| Metrics | Bandwidth, latency, status codes | Wellbeing score, community value (Vcom), reputation earned |
| Data Structure | Typically involves headers and payload in JSON or HTML | Time slot submission with context (start/end time, wellbeing, skills, community) |
| Monetization | Ads, subscriptions, and content delivery | Labor equity: rewards (reputation, points, wellbeing improvements, VPoints) |
| Security | HTTPS (encryption via SSL/TLS) | Privacy via decentralized control, wellbeing data protected per individual |
| Extensibility | Extensible through headers and methods (cookies, sessions) | Open protocol stack extensible via DAOcommons, wellbeing improvements, and skill validation |
| Time Component | Requests are stateless and independent of time | Time-dependent value capture: Start and end time dictate value contribution |
| Request Format | Method (GET, POST, etc.), URL, headers, body | SubmitTimeSlot action: Start time, end time, activity description, wellbeing context, proof of work |
| Response Format | Status code, headers, body | Validation result, value captured (wellbeing, community value, VPoints) |
| Impact on Individuals | Content consumers (indirectly benefiting from services) | Direct contributors: time, skills, and wellbeing are tracked and rewarded |
| Community Aspect | Not community-centric, client-server architecture | Community-centric: collaboration through learning, earning, and community-building activities |

#### **VHTTP Request (Submit Time Slot)**
